title: Errors: throw, try/catch/finally and the Error objects

videos.script:
You have read a lot of error messages in this course. {{read}} A name, a message, and a list of lines under it. Today you learn to produce them on purpose, and to decide where they should be caught.

{{throw}} Throwing an error says: this function cannot do what it was asked, and the caller needs to know. It stops the function on the spot and travels back up through every caller until something catches it.

{{catch}} Catching is the harder half. Catch too little and one bad record stops a whole program. Catch too much and an error disappears, and a bug that would have taken five minutes to find takes a day, because the place it happened says nothing.

{{types}} You will meet the built-in kinds, TypeError, RangeError and the rest, and make your own, so code can tell an overdue loan from a broken card. {{async}} And you will see the one place a try block cannot reach: an error thrown later, in a callback.
